title: TypeScript SDK: bridging async generators and Web Streams with deterministic cancellation semantics
creator: Owen Carter
description: Goal: Provide a small, well-tested bridging layer in the TypeScript SDK that makes it safe and ergonomic to consume Redwood streaming responses as either async generators (AsyncIterable) or Web Streams (ReadableStream) with well-defined and deterministic cancellation semantics. Rationale: Customers and downstream integrations expect both consumption models depending on runtime (Node, Deno, Browser) and application needs (server backpressure vs browser pump). Existing examples are fragmented and lead to subtle token leaks, unpropagated cancellation, and inconsistent retry behavior when a consumer abandons a stream. This ticket is to design, implement, and document a unified adapter and examples that handle: graceful cancellation, backpressure propagation where available, abort signal wiring, idempotent retries for short-lived failures, and clear migration guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes two ergonomic helpers: toAsyncIterable(readable: ReadableStream|ReadableStreamDefaultReader, signal?: AbortSignal) and toWebStream(asyncIterable: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>|AsyncIterable<string>, options?: { highWaterMark?: number, signal?: AbortSignal })
Cancellation from the consumer triggers immediate upstream cancellation and releases KV cache/connection resources within 150ms in local tests
Retries on transient network errors integrate with consumer cancellation (i.e., if consumer cancels during retry backoff, retry aborts immediately)
Comprehensive examples for Node + Browser + Deno demonstrating both consumption modes and showing how to combine with SDK retry policies
Unit and integration tests covering edge cases: mid-chunk cancellation, double-cancel, reader.releaseLock() patterns, and resumed consumption after benign pauses
Docs and migration guide published to /docs/sdk/ts/streaming and a short console demo in the examples repo
activity: 2025-02-12 — Ticket created by Owen Carter. Initial investigation: prototype adapter in playground that wraps ReadableStreamDefaultReader into AsyncGenerator. Observed GC leak when AbortController not forwarded to underlying fetch in Node. Linked notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1example-design-notes

2025-02-13 — Spike by Asha Patel: implemented minimal adapter (40 LOC) and benchmarked on local harness. Observed cancellation delay ~400ms due to fetch polyfill not honoring AbortController in older Node runtime. Logged PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4412 (WIP)

2025-02-14 — Design review with Marcus Nguyen and Elena Rossi. Decisions: (1) require SDK consumers to pass optional AbortSignal to all streaming helpers; (2) adapter will create an internal AbortController when not provided and expose a cancel() helper for convenience; (3) retry logic will be cancellable by wiring AbortSignals into backoff timers. Trade-offs: we avoid implicit global signal to reduce accidental resource retention, but it increases call-site ergonomics slightly. See short writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/TS+Streaming+Bridge

2025-02-15 — Engineering note: chosen approach uses a small shim that uses ReadableStreamDefaultReader.read() loop for browsers and stream.getReader() in Node when available; falls back to async generator consumption using the WHATWG stream piping API in Node 18+. This hybrid ensures best-effort backpressure when platform supports it.

2025-02-16 — Added tests for mid-chunk cancellation and double-cancel scenarios. Found an edge where reader.releaseLock() followed by a new reader could result in lost abort propagation. Fixed by attaching a shared AbortSignal internally and rejecting subsequent reads with a CancelledError. Tests added: tests/streaming/adapter-cancel.spec.ts

2025-02-17 — PR updated to include instrumentation hooks for Console metrics and example trace spans (stream.open, stream.cancel, stream.finish). Early benchmarks show 8% overhead vs raw fetch stream in Node when instrumentation enabled; disabled by default. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4412 (ready for review)

2025-02-18 — UX pass with Design: added example snippets showing three common patterns: fire-and-forget UI streaming (browser), server-side pipelining to file (Node), and progressive decoding with structured tokens. Design suggested clearer naming for helpers; updated API names accordingly.

2025-02-19 — Security/QA: ran fuzz test harness that simulates flaky network and rapid cancel-retry loops. Found rare race in retry+cancel where backoff timer resolved after AbortSignal fired; fixed by checking signal state before scheduling retry. Coordinating release notes and docs.

2025-02-20 — Status update: branch passes CI, integration tests green on Node 18 and Chrome headless. Preparing final review and changelog entry for sdk-2025.02 release. Next steps: add TypeDoc comments, record short demo video, and schedule a small migration office hours session with early beta customers.
notes: Implementation languages: TypeScript, targeting builds for ESM (Node 18+), Deno, and Browser bundles
Backpressure strategy: leverage platform readers when available; for older runtimes emulate soft backpressure with queued chunks and highWaterMark

Retry semantics: retries only for idempotent operations or temporary connection failures; documented behavior for streaming endpoints that produce partial progress (we default to fail-fast unless caller opts into automatic resume semantics)
Testing: unit tests for the adapter, integration tests hitting a local mock server that streams tokenized JSON, and e2e test with Playwright for the browser example
Migration guidance: provide code snippets that replace manual adapter code in customer repos; highlight common pitfalls (not forwarding AbortSignal, not calling reader.cancel())
